target: Existence and exactly one weak right-equivalence class of nondegenerate completed potentials for all tagged triangulations of every closed oriented genus g >= 1 surface with two punctures, over every algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic.

dependencies.role: Prior published resolution; Section 2 elimination and Section 4 uniqueness checked with the explicit authored local corrections.

dependencies.source: Labardini-Fragoso, Removing boundary assumptions, Theorem 8.1 and Corollary 9.1
dependencies.role: Explicit surface-potential existence and nondegeneracy, and tagged-flip compatibility without characteristic or uncountability restrictions.
Finite tagged-flip connectivity for the two-puncture target; the different exclusion in Theorem 7.11 is not imported.

dependencies.source: Derksen–Weyman–Zelevinsky, Quivers with potentials and their representations I, Proposition 2.4 and Theorems 4.6, 5.2, 5.7
dependencies.role: Complete-algebra automorphisms, splitting, well-defined mutation and involutivity; scalar rescaling supplies weak-equivalence transport.

dependencies.source: Labardini-Fragoso, Quivers with potentials associated to triangulated surfaces, Proposition 21 and Corollary 22
dependencies.role: Restriction preserves nondegeneracy. The induced-cycle coefficient necessity is then checked directly over arbitrary fields.

dependencies.source: Geiss–Labardini-Fragoso–Schröer, The representation type of Jacobian algebras, Proposition 2.4, Corollary 2.5 and Lemma 8.5
dependencies.role: C-based source statements are explicitly limited; the needed arbitrary-field cycle implication and algebraically closed coefficient normalization are supplied in the authored audit.

dependencies.source: Labardini-Fragoso, Removing boundary assumptions, Lemma 2.4 and Proposition 10.4
dependencies.role: Convergent unitriangular limits and algebraically closed coefficient equivalence; the present audit also gives compatible inverse maps and a direct nonzero-root normalization.
Explicit all-genus mate indexing, formal splitting, field-independent cycle test, zero-series conventions, convergence estimates and coefficient scaling. No novelty or priority claim.

limitations: No uniqueness claim for ordinary right equivalence without a nonzero scalar.
No uniqueness claim over arbitrary non-algebraically-closed fields.
No uniqueness claim for degenerate potentials or for one-puncture surfaces.
The C-based GLS statements are not silently promoted to arbitrary-field representation-type theorems; the needed cycle-necessity implication is proved directly.
Generic uncountable-field existence is not used to cover countable algebraically closed fields.
Imported published theorems are applied at checked hypotheses, not re-proved in full generality.
Finite genera, characteristic and exponent checks are supplementary, not an infinite proof.
No author-issued erratum, external human peer review, formal machine proof, novelty or priority is claimed.
